claims.statement: The agent layer call chain routes identity through two successive RFC 8693 token exchanges: the BFF's confidential agent-subject-token client exchanges the member's session access token for a short-TTL, run-scoped, audience-narrowed delegation token handed to the Agent Gateway as a non-checkpointed value, and the gateway's shared MCP client exchanges that again for a further-downscoped, aud=mc-service, <=60s token attached only to the individual tool call.

The BFF hosts CopilotRuntime plus the AG-UI HttpAgent (from @ag-ui/client) wired to a vendored ExperimentalEmptyAdapter, performing no LLM call or orchestration itself, because the LangGraph runtime already emits AG-UI events natively; using LangGraphHttpAgent instead would 404 because it speaks the LangGraph Platform REST protocol, not AG-UI.

A paused HITL run holds no token at all, only checkpointed graph state plus userId/threadId; because every resume is itself an authenticated BFF request, the BFF supplies a fresh run-scoped subject token on every resume, which is why token lifetime is decoupled from pause duration.

Per-user agent config (feature 018) is off by default, AES-256-GCM-encrypted at rest in the BFF-owned mcm-bff-db (physically separate from mc-db), decrypted only in-memory per run via resolveForRun(userId), and forwarded to the gateway via the X-Agent-Config header; the CopilotKit dock mounts only for a runnable config (enabled + provider credential + TMDB key).

The user-supplied Ollama base URL is SSRF-guarded independently in two processes: the BFF's agent-config-ssrf.ts and the gateway's src/ollama_guard.py (invoked from models.py), because a check made in one process can be stale by the time the other process opens the connection.

Feature 059 extended the add flow's stage chain to awaiting_childrens -> awaiting_ownership -> awaiting_media -> awaiting_ripped -> awaiting_rip_quality -> proposal, placing the children's question first because the 047 media/ripped/rip-quality questions are conditional on ownership and any later placement would skip them for a not-owned add.

A refused run-scoped subject-token mint fails closed: Keycloak rejecting the member's credential yields 401 AGENT_IDENTITY_REJECTED (client renews once, then sign-in) and an outage, timeout or non-credential error yields retryable 503 AGENT_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE, with the gateway never called identity-less. Keycloak 26.5 answers a revoked or malformed subject token with 400 invalid_request "Invalid token" rather than the RFC's invalid_token, and that exact description is required because invalid_request is also used for configuration faults that are outages, not credential rejections.

Since feature 085 the member's Keycloak access and refresh tokens never reach the client: they are sealed with AES-256-GCM beside the Redis session, bound to the session id and owner, and renewed by the BFF itself at most once per session at a time behind a short Redis lock (a second concurrent renewal would fail because Keycloak rotates refresh tokens). The client holds exactly one credential, the opaque mcm_session_id cookie, and a bearer credential presented to the BFF is refused in every environment.

The gateway's per-call downscoped token is obtained by an OPA authorization check followed by the re-exchange and an in-memory (user, audience) cache; the cache expires entries 15 seconds ahead of the reported lifetime because expires_in is measured at mint time while mc-service validates the JWT's real exp, a skew added after a long bulk apply hit clustered 401s at each TTL boundary.

OPA authorizes each token exchange with non-sensitive inputs only (user_id, audience, agent_origin) and fails closed when OPA_URL is set (any deny, non-2xx, malformed response or unreachable engine denies), while an unset OPA_URL skips the check with a warning; the exchange itself sends no audience parameter, relying instead on the agent-gateway client's audience mappers to stamp aud=[movie-collection-manager, mc-service] so the unchanged mc-service accepts the token while mc-service remains the agent-origin binding signal.

The downscoped token is never an LLM-visible tool argument: it is injected as the MCP request's Authorization Bearer header by a dynamic httpx auth object reading a request-local ContextVar set synchronously just before the call, and it is injected per request rather than as a client default header so a credential-bearing auth object cannot outlive its call.

The no-token-in-checkpointed-state invariant is enforced in code, not just documented: state.forbid_token_fields raises before any state is persisted when a top-level state key's name looks like a credential (token, jwt, authorization, bearer, secret, password, credential, api_key, apikey, agent_config), and an AST token-leak scan over the agent and MCP source trees fails the unit tier on a logged token-named variable.

The BFF binds each CopilotKit thread_id to the first user who uses it (Redis SET NX, TTL equal to the session's absolute window) and refuses any later cross-user use with 403 before the gateway is reached, closing a preview-disclosure gap where a user presenting another user's thread_id could read the checkpointed proposal even though cross-user writes were already blocked by DAC.

Every per-run value the BFF supplies to the gateway rides as an HTTP header (Authorization, X-UI-Snapshot, X-Import-File, X-Agent-Config), is captured into request-local ContextVars by pure-ASGI middlewares, and is bridged into config["configurable"] at IdentityAwareAGUIAgent.prepare_stream, because a ContextVar set at the ASGI boundary does not reliably propagate into LangGraph's per-node executor tasks.

The BFF classifies each agent POST as a billable LLM run or a non-billable CopilotKit handshake read by GraphQL operationName, defaulting to billable; only a billable run resolves the per-user config, enforces the cost ceiling and accrues the turn estimate, while the rate limit and cross-user thread guard apply to every POST, and the UI-snapshot and single-use import-file bridges are gated on the same billable signal so a handshake cannot consume a pending upload.

The per-run agent config header carries only the four gateway-relevant fields (provider, ollamaBaseUrl, anthropicKey, tmdbKey) — the per-user costLimitUsd stays BFF-only — and the TMDB key is additionally attached out-of-band as X-TMDB-Key only around web-api-mcp calls, so it is never sent to a user-identity MCP server.

The canonical search-cancel control is routed in the supervisor before the classifier call, above the classifier's exception handler and the error-rate breaker, but below the kill switch: an escape hatch that can be classified away, or that depends on a healthy provider, is not an escape hatch. It is also refused while an add stage is live, and the stage-free route matches the whole message exactly (trimmed, case-folded) rather than by substring or bare synonyms, which would hijack a real title or steal the cancel reply from the import and organize flows.

Every stage-continuation guard in the supervisor is paired with a matching *_STATE_RESET, an ownership-stage reply is resolved against the pending question BEFORE the classified intent is consulted (otherwise a prose-like answer such as "Selected: none" classifies as query/search and silently discards the in-progress flow), and the curator carries its own copy of the ownership-stage passthrough set so an add's bare answer is not run through entity extraction — meaning a new stage requires updating both graph.py's guard and curator.py's passthrough.

The generic degrade reply has exactly two sources — the supervisor's classifier raising and the breaker already being open — while the curator, organizer and query degrade sites fail on the specialist model; ErrorRateBreaker is fed by exactly one signal, circuit.record(...) in the supervisor, so an open breaker always means the supervisor's model call is failing and never that a tool, MCP server or rate limiter failed.

The import flow checkpoints only a small opaque import_handle across clarification turns, with the parsed spreadsheet stashed once in spreadsheet-mcp's transient store and its TTL refreshed on every read, because re-serializing the whole parsed workbook per turn was the checkpoint bloat behind a large import timing out; the upload store is single-use while the parsed-handle store is not.

An assistant-added movie's rated value is the film's real first non-empty US certification from an appended TMDB release_dates block, validated against {G, PG, PG-13, R, NC-17, NR, Unrated}, and an unknown certification becomes a present "rated": null key rather than an omitted key or a substituted "NR" — omitting it 422s the add because CreateMovieDto types rated as Option without serde(default), and there is deliberately no PG-13 to PG13 rename because mc-service rejects the unhyphenated form.

Three distinct generative-UI selection tools exist with fixed names: render_selection (selection-options) serves the navigator clarify, import picks, search scope, the 040/047 ownership Yes/No and the 059 children's Yes/No; render_disambiguation (disambiguation-options) serves only the curator's ambiguous movie-candidate list; render_multi_select (multi-select-options) serves only the 047 media-format and rip-quality toggles.

LangFuse, OpenTelemetry/Grafana, OPA and Unleash run under the observability profile while the OpenSearch append-only audit sink runs under its own separate audit profile, and every one is env-gated to a no-op when unconfigured so the agent layer works in a plain dev environment with none of them running.

Agent test tiers encode three rules: a change touching routing, a guard or a *_stage must be driven through build_graph rather than a node function, because a node-level test bypasses every supervisor guard and stage check; a build_runtime_graph(force=True) test must stub all three model seams (extract, plan, query_extract) and set spreadsheet_mcp_url, or it passes while exercising nothing; and the integration tier must be run with MCM_REQUIRE_LIVE_STACK=1 because a skip caused by an unreachable MCP server otherwise reads as a pass.
